propositions: Compaction rollback on reverse-rename failure logs the error but unconditionally deletes the snapshot, leaving reversed sources invisible and violating the all-or-none contract.

The fix retains the snapshot on rollback failure because it already carries the folded effect; fsck's existing SNAPSHOT_INCONSISTENT detection and --repair-snapshots rebuild path can reconcile the mixed state.
Reads in the mixed state (before repair) are correct because normal replay short-circuits on the snapshot and skips pre-snapshot events, preventing double-count of the reversed-to-active source.
Fault-injection tests must cover forward-rename failures (all sources restored, clean fsck) and reverse-rename failures (snapshot retained, diagnostic emitted, no data loss).
The fsck --repair-snapshots path rebuilds the snapshot and renames formerly-active sources to *.retired; the repair test must assert new snapshot is written and a follow-up fsck exits clean.
